byzantineempireirl: Walter Byzantineemp walked into S-S9 on Day 5 and asked where the war was. A shell answered before anyone else could.
Walter Byzantineemp borrowed a serial novel from a newspaper bundle. The instalment ends with a locked door and a pistol shot. The next issue is missing.
jasmandeep_singh999: Felix "Tin" Singh signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at S-F5 took him in like it takes everyone: without a word.
A round came through a gap in the sandbags at S-F5 and grazed Felix "Tin" Singh's arm. Two inches, the sergeant said. Shot by Felix Szymanski of the Hegemony (@franek.szymanski.376).
Felix "Tin" Singh no longer winces when he lifts his rifle. The medic signed him off with a grunt.

Out on the wire with the wiring party. A bullet clipped Felix "Tin" Singh's helmet at S-F5 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. A letter from home reached Felix "Tin" Singh before dusk. Felix "Tin" Singh read it twice and slept a little easier.
kamdensipple: Otto "Saint" Kamdensipple walked into S-F6 on Day 3 and asked where the war was. A shell answered before anyone else could. Orders came through: Otto "Saint" Kamdensipple is a sniper now. He handed in his old kit and kept only a rosary of rough beads.
A clear shot from S-F6. Otto "Saint" Kamdensipple grazed Leopold "Doc" Cornkkob and slid back down below the parapet.
Otto "Saint" Kamdensipple found a clean spot on the table and set his bread on it. Within a minute, someone asked to borrow the spot.
Dawn watch. Otto "Saint" Kamdensipple put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Bram "Crow" Mitaylor, badly wounded.
seamus_bj: The new sniper gave his name as Norbert Seamus. The corporal looked at his boots, then at the mud, and laughed for the first time in a week.
A bullet went through Norbert Seamus's sleeve at S-F19 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Emil Ghostbebrii of the Hegemony (@ghostbebrii).

Norbert Seamus no longer winces when he lifts his rifle. The medic signed him off with a grunt. A letter from home reached Norbert Seamus before dusk. Norbert Seamus read it twice and slept a little easier.

A newspaper reached Norbert Seamus with the corner torn off. According to the half a sentence that survived, the war was going well. A letter from home reached Norbert Seamus before dusk. Norbert Seamus read it twice and slept a little easier.
vis.acquillae: Edmund Acquillae left a teacher who said he would amount to nothing behind in Halden and came up the line with a stub of a pencil. The men noticed at once that he polishes his buttons every evening.
Volunteer number 34. The quartermaster pinned the First Wave ribbon on Edmund Acquillae's tunic and said: 'Don't let the mud have it.'
Edmund Acquillae asked to leave the riflemans and serve as a signaller. The sergeant looked at him for a long time, then signed the paper without a word.
Edmund Acquillae was promised a surprise at supper. It was an extra potato. He accepted the surprise with proper ceremony.

Edmund Acquillae taught Silas Zdsh to play the harmonica. The bay has asked them both, formally, to stop. Day 3: Verdel Ridge was lost. Edmund Acquillae wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
Edmund Acquillae dreamt about missing a train. Waking up here felt like a harsh punishment for it.

A direct hit on the trench at S-F10. Edmund Acquillae was the only one they could still help, and only just. Edmund Acquillae was killed outright by a direct hit at S-F10. The men dug for an hour and found only his identity disc.

Isidor Acquillae joined S-F10 under the shadow of Edmund Acquillae's name. At the first roll call, the corporal used the right one. Isidor Acquillae received the First Wave ribbon. He checked the stitching twice before putting the tunic back on. Now serving as a signaller, Isidor Acquillae discovered that being experienced at the front did not prevent being new at the job.

Isidor Acquillae spent the night in no man's land with pliers and a roll of wire. Every flare meant lying flat in the mud. The gap at S-F10 is closed now. Isidor Acquillae raised his head for a heartbeat too long at S-F10. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Wendel "Mole" Day of the Concord (@selfie_and_mugs_every_day2.0). Mail came up the line with a letter for Isidor Acquillae. Isidor Acquillae read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
